[Documentation] The Javadoc now says “DO NOT USE OR OVERRIDE THIS METHOD”, but `SqlClientAttributesExtractor` explicitly allows custom `getDbOperationName()` implementations to override the parsed value (see comment around `DbClientAttributesExtractor.onStartCommon(...)` call). This wording is misleading for instrumentation authors and contradicts the extractor behavior.

Consider rewording to explain that the extractor can derive `db.operation.name` from SQL text when `setSingleOperationAndCollection(true)` is enabled, and that overriding is optional and takes precedence when provided.

threads.body:
[Documentation] Same issue as `getDbOperationName()`: the Javadoc says not to use/override `getDbCollectionName()`, but the extractor code is designed so that an explicit getter implementation can override the parsed `db.collection.name` when `setSingleOperationAndCollection(true)` is enabled. The current wording is likely to confuse implementers.

Reword to describe the default behavior (derived from SQL parsing) and when overriding makes sense.

[Bug] In stable semconv, the SQL span-name fallback when `analyzedQuery.getQuerySummary()` is null currently ignores `analyzedQuery.getOperationName()` and `analyzedQuery.getCollectionName()`. That can produce low-information span names (e.g., falling back to `db.namespace` / `db.system.name`) even though the analyzer already extracted operation + target and stable semconv’s primary naming format is `{db.operation.name} {db.collection.name}`.

It seems safer to use the parsed operation/collection when available before falling back to stored procedure / namespace / server address.

replies.body: The `analyzeWithSummary` analyzer only records `operationName`/`collectionName` together with the query summary — every `recordOperationName()` in the JFlex grammar is paired with an `appendOperationToSummary()`, and `getResult()` returns `summary = querySummaryBuilder.length() > 0 ? ... : null`. So when `getQuerySummary()` is null, the operation and collection names are also null. This fallback is only reached in that "nothing was parsed" case, so passing `getOperationName()`/`getCollectionName()` here would be dead code.

threads.body: Grammar fix: change 'still use' to 'still uses' in the comment.

Including `DB_COLLECTION_NAME` unconditionally in `hasDurationMetric()` will fail when stable database semconv is disabled, since that attribute is not expected to be emitted in legacy mode. Make the expected attribute key set conditional on `emitStableDatabaseSemconv()` (e.g., only include `DB_COLLECTION_NAME` when stable semconv is enabled).

threads.body: `emitStableDatabaseSemconv()` is evaluated multiple times in the same assertion block, which hurts readability and makes it easier for the logic to drift over time. Consider storing the result in a local boolean (e.g., `boolean stable = emitStableDatabaseSemconv();`) and using that for the conditional branches.
